title: Instacart Builds Blueberry, an AI-Powered Assistant to Help On-Call Engineers Investigate Incidents
gist: Instacart runs Blueberry, a multi-agent AI incident-response assistant that fires ~10 subagents in parallel on alert and posts a grounded root-cause hypothesis into the Slack thread within about three minutes. Grounding it in more than 14 years of internal incident history lifted diagnostic accuracy from the mid-60% range to the high 90s, and at ~25,000 diagnostic passes in April it demonstrates that operational context and tool harness, not raw model capability, decide whether ops AI works.

insights.claim: Instacart built its incident assistant to attack a specific bottleneck: engineers spend the early stages of an incident collecting context — service ownership, deployments, logs, metrics, docs and prior incidents — before diagnosis can even start.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The monetizable wedge in ops AI is context assembly, not autonomous fixing — vendors selling retrieval across telemetry and ownership data address the real time sink.
insights.locator: The system was built to address a common challenge in large-scale operations

insights.claim: Instacart's assistant changes the on-call starting point from an empty investigation path to a pre-populated one containing logs, deployments and related system information, according to Director of Software Engineering Alan Wong.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Value accrues at the front of the incident timeline, which is where mean-time-to-mitigate is actually decided.
insights.locator: Alan Wong, Director of Software Engineering at Instacart, highlighted

insights.claim: Blueberry runs inside Slack-based incident workflows so engineers investigate without leaving the collaboration channel they already work in.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Chat-native delivery, not a new console, is the adoption pattern for ops AI — a distribution advantage for whoever owns the incident channel.
insights.locator: Blueberry integrates with Slack-based incident workflows

themes.theme: Proprietary incident history as the accuracy lever

insights.claim: Grounding the system in more than 14 years of internal incident history moved diagnostic accuracy from the mid-60% range to the high 90% range at Instacart.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A ~30-point accuracy jump from proprietary history says the defensible asset is a company's own operational archive, not the model — favoring incumbents with long telemetry retention.
insights.locator: The company attributed improvements in diagnostic accuracy

insights.claim: Rather than relying only on general-purpose language models, the architecture connects agents to internal sources such as incident history, service ownership data, logs, deployments and other debugging signals.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Off-the-shelf LLM ops products without deep internal-system integration should be expected to underperform in-house builds on accuracy.
insights.locator: The architecture combines AI reasoning with organization-specific operational knowledge

insights.claim: Effective AI systems for operations depend not only on model capability but on the surrounding engineering framework — operational context, specialized workflows, tool integrations and feedback loops.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: The scarce input in enterprise AI is integration engineering, which shifts spend toward platform teams and away from model licenses.

insights.claim: Incorporating historical incidents and team-specific context makes prior operational experience retrievable during future investigations, turning tribal incident knowledge into a reusable asset.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Knowledge retention lowers the cost of engineer turnover, a quiet operating-leverage argument for AI in ops.
insights.locator: The system also focuses on preserving operational knowledge

insights.claim: When an alert fires, Instacart's Blueberry launches roughly 10 subagents in parallel and posts a grounded root-cause hypothesis directly into the Slack thread, typically within about three minutes, per CTO Anirban Kundu.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: A concrete latency and fan-out benchmark for agentic ops systems — three minutes to a hypothesis is the bar competing tools must beat.
insights.locator: According to Kundu, when an alert is triggered

insights.claim: Blueberry uses a durable, tool-aware harness with a production path plus a side-mounted MCP catalog, persisted state and a reviewed-improvement loop, so agents retrieve from connected systems while maintaining investigation state.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: MCP is showing up as production plumbing at scale, not a demo protocol — relevant to anyone betting on agent tool-integration standards.
insights.locator: Durable, tool-aware harness: production path plus side-mounted MCP catalog

insights.claim: Instacart's CTO frames Blueberry as part of a broader corporate exploration of agentic AI systems rather than a one-off SRE tool.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Incident response is being used as the beachhead workload for broader agentic deployment inside large engineering orgs.
insights.locator: Instacart CTO Anirban Kundu described Blueberry

insights.claim: Blueberry deliberately assists by gathering information, generating hypotheses and supporting debugging, and does not automatically make production changes.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Even at 99.9% workflow success, a large operator refuses write access to production — the realistic near-term ceiling for autonomous remediation claims.
insights.locator: The system assists engineers by gathering information

insights.claim: Engineers at Instacart remain responsible for diagnosis, mitigation decisions and remediation, with the AI system positioned as a force multiplier rather than a replacement.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Headcount displacement in SRE is not the immediate story; throughput per on-call engineer is.
insights.quote: Blueberry has proven to be a force multiplier in harnessing AI to help transform on-call and help us quickly troubleshoot and mitigate complex issues in production.
insights.locator: Siby Alappatt, Vice President of Engineering at Instacart

insights.claim: Instacart reported roughly 25,000 diagnostic passes in April across more than 270 Slack channels, a scale that indicates fleet-wide deployment rather than a pilot.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Real usage volume is the signal that separates production agentic AI from vendor demos when evaluating similar claims.
insights.locator: Instacart reported that Blueberry executed approximately 25,000 diagnostic passes

insights.claim: In one month the system logged a reported 99.9% workflow success rate, more than 58,000 MCP tool dispatches and support for around 60 team profiles.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: 58,000 monthly tool dispatches at one company hints at the token and tool-call volume enterprise agent workloads will drive through inference providers.
insights.locator: The system processed approximately 25,000 diagnostic passes in one month
